reason: The NEON transpose proposal is first because it changes the timed conversion in the measured TB path, which scored below controls; those results do not isolate transpose cost, so any benefit remains unverified. The 288-byte scratch layout is distinct from the rejected 272-byte layout, but cache geometry and benefit are unknown. Half-band packing has substantial traversal and repacking risk, and TA adds a timed transpose while retaining generated B packing and adding A packing. Four-step unrolling extends the unpromoted two-step experiment. The fused transpose repeats A-tile conversion across 16 column panels. The proposed K-pair schedule appears to duplicate the measured two-step unroll, so it ranks last pending proof of a distinct instruction schedule.
